fossil
The papersThe code

A mutation predictor benchmark, dug back up.

Martelotto and colleagues scored 15 mutation effect predictors, and 11,253 ways of combining them, on 989 cancer mutations whose effect is known. Their statistics code was never shared. We rebuilt it from the paper as the package mutbench and reran it on their own spreadsheet.

Optimal n and p (Results)Differs0 of 0 values (2 paper slips left out)
  • for n = 1 to 4, the best p is about 2n: paper yes, ours no
  • for p = 3 to 11, the best n is about p/2: paper yes, ours no
Both sentences have n and p swapped: the paper's own Additional file 25, and our run, give a best n of about 2p (p about n/2), capped at all 11 predictors. Our run gives the same optimal p and n as Additional file 25 for 20 of 21 rows (af25). Additional file 25 (B) gives p = 1, 1, 2 for n = 2, 3, 4: the best p is about n/2 (n about 2p), as the next sentence's 'n approximately p/2' would say were it also reversed. p <= n everywhere, so p about 2n cannot hold.; Additional file 25 (A) gives n = 6, 7, 9, 10 for p = 3 to 6 and n = 11 (all predictors) for p = 7 to 11: the best n is about 2p, capped at 11. n >= p everywhere, so n about p/2 cannot hold.

The main finding holds: no single predictor is accurate enough, and combining CHASM (breast) with MutationTaster gives the best accuracy, composite score and NPV, in both subsets, as the paper says. The claims that do not match move with the random splits, or are the paper's own slips.

What stayed buried

  • The authors' code. It was never released; the method is rebuilt from the text.
  • The exact random splits and resamples. Counts of combinations near a cutoff and the order of near ties move with them: 1,854 combinations beat FATHMM (cancer) in both subsets in the paper and in our run, and 6 of them significantly in the paper, 5 in ours.
  • Two sentences on the optimal n and p have n and p swapped. The paper's own Additional file 25 agrees with our run, not with the sentences.
  • Additional file 8 leaves out Mutation Assessor's 7 N/A calls; Additional file 9 counts them as low confidence.
  • Additional file 2 swaps the headers of FATHMM's two training-set columns. We read them by their content.

The main finding holds: no single predictor is accurate enough, and combining CHASM (breast) with MutationTaster gives the best accuracy, composite score and NPV, in both subsets, as the paper says. The claims that do not match move with the random splits, or are the paper's own slips.
